parole.testo: From Middle High German hafer, haber, hafere, habere, from Old High German habaro. The modern consonantism is Central German (compare Middle Low German haver, havere and modern German Low German Haver, Hafer). The Upper German cognate form Haber is now obsolete in standard usage.

parole.significato: skin, peel (mostly in reference to sausages or vegetables, especially potatoes)
parole.testo: From Middle Low German *pelle, whose existence is assured by the word’s prevalence in eastern dialects of German Low German (and East Central German). It was introduced there by Dutch settlers from Middle Dutch pelle, an old borrowing from Latin pellis (“skin”). Compare modern Dutch pel, pellen.
